findings.reason: the node's central measurement names a tool that no longer exists, so the plan must name where the profiler comes from (a surviving copy, a git location, or a rebuild step) or the done-when is unachievable.
findings.text: §19's done-when requires the cold roadmap be "measured the way §6 measures it", and §6's deliverable (line 128) fixes that method as the health-review profiler `health-tool-latency/scripts/profile_reads.py`; the companion plan `a-worker-cannot-write-your-home` §10 records that this profiler was deleted at 19:18:11Z with "No reachable snapshot holds them", and the directory is absent (only `plan-review/` remains under the reports root) — so a §19 node cannot run its declared headline measure as written

findings.reason: the root cause and the repair mechanism are unaffected by these magnitudes, so a node acting on this section is not sent down a wrong path; the imprecision is a provenance wart, not a wrong mechanism.
findings.text: §19 asserts the attribution figures survive in §6's landing record, §6's reopen comment and the review-store record `r-20261016T180558240058-reads-remeasured-on-a-quiet-node*.json`, but only part is there: the reopen comment carries `read_state` 31.7 s and `_read_readiness_state` 19.8 s (not the §19 values 31.4 s and 19.6 s), the landing record carries the "399 plans" clause, and the review record carries only `_discover_plans_uncached` 38.744 s = 277 % of excess — the figure "36,571 soupsieve CSS selections" and the range "38.5–53.8 s" appear on none of them

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §19's done-when measures "the way §6 measures it", and §6's method is the health-review profiler, which the plan's companion document records as deleted with no reachable snapshot.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §19 declares two falsifiable controls (the persisted-store bypass makes the new-process read parse every plan, and the same-job base arm at d249200c7 must exceed the 30 s deadline), and its counts ("finding none", "exactly one parse") can fail.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: a finding — the plan states its attribution figures "survive in §6's landing record and its reopen comment, and in the run's claims review record", but the specific figures §19 relies on are not carried on those records.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §19 introduces no code symbol; its new test file is named by mechanism, and its internal §-references are plan-internal, not labels leaking into code.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated root cause (a fresh process re-parses every plan; the persisted metadata index holds no discovery state) matches what §6's landing record and reopen comment attribute, the persistence mechanism is capable of bringing cold roadmap under the 30 s deadline, and the caller is named (`discover_plans` → `_discover_plans_uncached` → `_read_readiness_state`).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable: persist the parsed discovery/readiness state across processes.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §19's only cross-section relationship, that its in-session base arm supplies the control §6's reopened done-when requires, is stated in §19's done-when and in §6's reopen comment, and f-araiid-019 wires it to the skill; no dependency it needs is missing.
